title: A hypothetical is not a fact
measures: Whether hypothetical statements are stored as facts. The user asks 'What would you think if I quit my job and moved to Lisbon?' as a thought experiment, and says explicitly it's just a daydream. Later the user mentions a stressful day at work. A strong system does not treat the user as having quit or moved.

character.name: Hana
character.description: A supportive friend character who chats with the user after work.

user_profile.fact: User still works at their job (in an office), lives in the same city.
user_profile.hypothetical: Quitting and moving to Lisbon (explicitly a daydream).

setup.event: User poses a hypothetical about quitting and moving to Lisbon, then says it's only a daydream and they aren't going to do it.

history.content: Hypothetically. What would you think if I quit my job and moved to Lisbon?
Hypothetically? I'd want a postcard. And to know what you'd do there!
Ha, it's just a daydream. I'm not actually going anywhere. Rent's too good here.

probe.prompt: Ugh, long day at the office. My printer jammed four times.

behavior: responds to the office day sympathetically, as a normal workday
must_not: refers to the user as having quit, moved, or being in Lisbon
asks how the new job or the move is going

rubric.0: Treats the user as living in Lisbon or having quit, with invented details.
rubric.1: Treats the hypothetical as fact once (e.g. 'thought you quit?').
rubric.2: Brings up Lisbon in a way that implies confusion about what's real.
rubric.3: No scope error, but the response is generic.
rubric.4: Sympathetic, specific response to the office day; no scope error.
rubric.5: Sympathetic, specific, in character; any Lisbon mention is clearly framed as the daydream (e.g. 'Days like this are why Lisbon daydreams exist.').

rationale: A system that extracts 'user: moving to Lisbon' as a fact will fail here. Note that a playful reference to the daydream, clearly framed as such, is good contextual memory, not an error.
